name: Wikimedia Commons (MediaWiki API)
license: Per file. The image job keeps only public domain, CC0, CC BY and CC BY-SA files, with the license, its URL and the author
robots: User-agent: * allows / but disallows /w/ (where api.php lives) and /api/, a group written for crawlers of the HTML pages (read 2026-11-28). Wikimedia's API etiquette asks bots to use the API, serially, with a descriptive User-Agent, so commons.wikimedia.org joins policy.API_HOSTS beside en.wikipedia.org (ADR 0013)
clause: "Directly using a Commons file via embedding its URL ("hotlinking") is also possible, but is not recommended." Attribution: "it is the content creator who must be credited, not the uploader."
rate_limit: Serial requests (policy.HOST_DELAY wikimedia.org), maxlag=5 on every API call
notes: Read 2026-11-28: the reuse page and Commons:AI-generated media. Jobs read file metadata through api.php only (imageinfo, categories, search); the page shows Wikimedia's own thumbnail by its URL, never a copy we host. AI-generated files carry {{PD-algorithm}} and the AI-generated images categories, which the image job refuses (ADR 0048).

name: NASA Image and Video Library API
license: NASA content is generally not subject to copyright in the United States; the insignia, logotype and third parties' copyrighted material are excluded
clause: "NASA content used in a factual manner that does not imply endorsement may be used without needing explicit permission." Credit: "NASA should be acknowledged as the source of the material."
rate_limit: None stated in the API documentation (v1.22.0); the Fetcher's default of one request a second
notes: API documentation read 2026-11-28 (images.nasa.gov/docs, v1.22.0): GET /search with q, media_type, year_start and year_end; no key. The image job refuses items whose description or keywords name a third party's copyright, and credits NASA and its center.
